title: Authenticated sessions end early
summary: Users are repeatedly returned to sign-in shortly after successfully opening protected pages, across both browser and mobile clients.
precursor: A session-policy adjustment was applied during the weekly identity configuration rollout; the application deployment remained unchanged.
impact: Staff must sign in multiple times during a shift, interrupting case handling and increasing help-desk reports of unexpected logouts.

title: New federated sign-ins are rejected
summary: Users who signed in recently receive authorization errors when opening connected applications, while some established sessions continue to work.
precursor: The identity provider completed scheduled federation maintenance shortly before the first reports from newly authenticated users.
impact: Newly authenticated staff cannot reach dependent applications, delaying approvals and leaving a growing queue of unprocessed requests.

title: Session renewal stalls at peak
summary: Sign-in succeeds, but token renewals become slow and intermittently fail during the morning traffic peak.
precursor: An inactive-account cleanup sweep overlapped with the start of the regional workday and a sharp rise in renewal traffic.
impact: Users experience repeated authentication prompts, while dependent APIs see bursts of rejected requests and elevated support volume.

title: Role changes appear inconsistently
summary: Access results disagree between the administration console and protected APIs after user roles change; some removed members retain access temporarily.
precursor: A directory synchronization completed a large role reconciliation, followed by a wave of access-policy updates.
impact: Security administrators cannot rely on immediate role changes, and support teams must verify access manually before sensitive work proceeds.

title: Federated login requests time out
summary: Federated sign-ins and session refreshes intermittently time out, although local health checks and non-authentication routes remain responsive.
precursor: The upstream identity provider reported a latency increase after regional maintenance, coinciding with the first rise in authentication failures.
impact: New users cannot reliably access the application and existing sessions fail to renew, reducing staff capacity across several internal tools.
